paper.title: From Declaration to Evidence: Research Provenance Card as Version-Bound Infrastructure for AI-Involved Research

activities.description: Framing of the problem, the decision to treat provenance as version-bound infrastructure rather than as a disclosure sentence, and final selection among competing designs.

Sustained adversarial critique of the author's framing during conceptual design, and proposal of design alternatives. Working-session logs exist but contain third-party unpublished material and personal data and are not releasable, so no artifact is referenced and the claim stays at the lowest level.

Retrieval and screening of candidate sources on publisher AI policies, reporting guidelines and provenance standards. Retrieved items were checked by the guarantor before use; the retrieval sessions themselves are not releasable.
Drafting of manuscript prose from the author's outline and decisions, across several revision rounds. The drafting sessions are part of the same non-releasable working log.
Read-through of the full manuscript, rewriting of claims, and removal of statements the guarantor could not stand behind.
Accountability for the manuscript and for this card, including the decision to lower the evidence level of three activities when the referenced log turned out not to be releasable.
